description:
Upstream states a validity range for only a handful of correlations: MatproZy
(273-1800 K), RelapZy (290-1800 K), MatproZy heat capacity (273-2099 K), IAEAZy
(273-2000 K), Banerjee (293-1273 K), SneadSiC (200-2400 K), Gehr (293 K cut-off),
IAEAZy density (1800 K), Zy emissivity (1500 K), Philipponneau (500 K lower
bound), HofmanD9, Tobbe, Watrous, and Lemehov's composition window.

Every other range in the port is a convention chosen by this crate, and each doc
comment says so explicitly rather than inventing a literature bound -- a test
asserts that no variant invents one.

Follow-up: source the real bounds from the literature (the oxide-fuel solidus
above all) and tighten them, replacing the port-chosen conventions. Until then
nobody should cite a range from this crate as a published limit.
title: offbeat: source real literature validity ranges for correlations where the port chose its own

acceptance_criteria: gpu_matches_cpu_reference passes for all 15 surface types on a GPU host at the existing tolerance, with no tolerance loosening.
description:
Unmasked by fixing op-bjd on 2026-08-06. Before that fix, probe() requested downlevel limits, surf_dist.bgl was rejected, and gpu_matches_cpu_reference never executed a single query — so this defect was invisible.

With real adapter limits sourced, the kernel runs and 13 of 15 surface types agree within the 1e-3*(1+|cpu|) tolerance. The TORUS types do not.

First divergence (NVIDIA RTX A5000 / NVK / Vulkan, 2026-08-06):
  query 16033 = surface 12 (XTorus), origin 10, direction 1
  gpu = 0.0000003120881   cpu = 0.49672258   |diff| = 0.49672228   tol = 0.0014967227

Decoding: the test batch is 27 origins x 48 directions = 1296 queries per surface, so query index / 1296 = surface index. Surface 12/13/14 are XTorus/YTorus/ZTorus.

The GPU returns a spurious near-ZERO root where the CPU finds a real crossing at 0.497 — a classic quartic root-finder failure mode (f32 conditioning in collect_real_roots_f32 / quartic_real_roots_f32, or the bisection bracket, or the coincident-epsilon guard). The WGSL is supposed to be a line-by-line translation of the Rust f32 mirror, so the two should agree far more tightly than this; a 0.5-cm disagreement is a logic divergence, not rounding.

Investigation entry points:
  - src/gpu/shaders/surface_distance.wgsl (torus + quartic path)
  - src/gpu/surface_distance.rs:451 quartic_real_roots_f32, :466 torus_distance_f32, :370 collect_real_roots_f32
  - The exact failing case is reproducible: XTorus{x0:0,y0:0,z0:0,a:1.0,b:0.3,c:0.3}, origin index 10, dir(1,48).

CURRENT STATE: gpu::surface_distance::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_reference FAILS on a GPU host. That is a real defect, not flakiness — do NOT loosen the tolerance to make it pass (workspace guardrail). The new hybrid test deliberately excludes tori so it tests work-splitting rather than this bug.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
ROOT CAUSE ESTABLISHED AND EXACTLY REPRODUCED, 2026-08-06. Three independent investigations converged.

MECHANISM (certain):
surface_distance.wgsl:298   let c0 = gc * gc - 4.0 * a2 * gamma;

For the failing ray the two operands are BIT-IDENTICAL f32 values (both 6.7599992752075195), i.e. 100% cancellation, all 24 mantissa bits lost. The true value is exactly 0 -- confirmed in exact rational arithmetic: gc^2 - 4*a2*gamma = 2.6^2 - 4*1.69 = 6.76 - 6.76 = 0.

- Rust does NOT contract mul+sub, so the CPU f32 mirror computes c0 = 0.0 exactly. The degenerate root stays at exactly 0 (measured -1.78e-15) and the t <= eps filter discards it. Correct answer 0.49672258 returned.
- The GPU backend IS permitted to fuse gc*gc - X into an FMA (one rounding instead of two), which keeps gc^2 exact and yields c0 = +2.2888184503244702e-07 -- about half an ULP of 6.76, a value not even representable as a difference of two f32 near 6.76.
- That perturbs the root at 0 to t = -c0/c1 = 3.1208810e-07. Running the full WGSL algorithm in float32 both ways:
    no FMA: c0=0           roots=[-1.78e-15, 0.49672258]  -> 4.967226e-01
    FMA:    c0=2.2888e-7   roots=[3.120881e-07, 0.49672228] -> 3.120881e-07
  EXACT match to the reported GPU value 3.120881e-7 (8 significant figures).

WHY THE ORIGIN MATTERS: the test origin (0,-1.3,0) lies EXACTLY on the torus outer equator (a+b = 1.0+0.3 = 1.3), so the quartic has an exact root at t=0 and c0 is exactly 0. The fixture passes coincident:false for a point that IS coincident.

THREE CONDITIONS, ALL TRUE:
1. Total cancellation makes c0 pure rounding noise whenever the origin is on the surface.
2. FMA contraction is legal AND UNCONTROLLABLE: grep -rn NoContraction over naga-29.0.3/29.0.4 returns NOTHING -- naga never emits the SPIR-V NoContraction decoration, so the driver is free to fuse. This is the entire CPU/GPU divergence; the algorithm is otherwise identical.
3. The filter at wgsl:302 is an ABSOLUTE eps = 1.0e-7, roughly 10x BELOW the measured f32 noise floor for this geometry: ulp(gc^2)/|c1| = 8e-7/0.733 = 1.1e-6. The f64 reference (geometry/surface.rs:880) uses 1e-10/1e-8; the f32 twin scaled eps by only 1000x while the noise floor grew by ~1e9x. Any c0 perturbation of half an ULP or more yields a root >= 1.6e-7, which ALWAYS passes.

Neither existing filter catches it: the spurious-branch test G(t) = +2.6 > 0 PASSES, so the fake root sits on the geometrically correct branch. The root-finder is NOT at fault -- it correctly returns a genuine root of the quartic it was handed.

EMPIRICAL SCOPE (independent agent, full 19440-query sweep on the real adapter):
- 79 mismatches / 19440 = 0.41%
- Non-torus surfaces 0-11: ZERO mismatches across 15552 queries. Completely clean.
- XTorus 70, ZTorus 9, YTorus 0.
- ALL 79 come from the 5 (surface, origin) pairs where the origin lies exactly on the torus (implicit residual 2.2e-16). Perfect correlation, no false positives or negatives.
- The GPU is NEVER larger and NEVER misses when the CPU hits. Every mismatch is a spurious tiny root: min 1.006e-7 (barely over the 1e-7 threshold), median 1.85e-7, max 3.5e-6.
- YTorus is clean ONLY because none of the 27 lattice origins happens to sit on it -- predicted from the mechanism alone: on-surface origin counts are XTorus 4/27, ZTorus 1/27, YTorus 0/27, exactly matching the observed failure pattern.
- The trusted f64 path agrees with the CPU f32 mirror in every case sampled (q16033: f64 = 4.96722659144033e-1, cpu_f32 = 4.9672258e-1, gpu = 3.12e-7). THE CPU IS THE CORRECT SIDE.

FIX CONSTRAINTS (things that will NOT work, established):
- Normalising the quartic changes nothing: c4 = ga^2 = 1.0 exactly here, the quartic is already monic, and all coefficients are O(1). Nothing overflows or underflows f32.
- Disabling FMA is not available: naga emits no NoContraction decoration.
- Reformulating c0 as a difference of squares (gc-2a*sqrt(gamma))(gc+2a*sqrt(gamma)) only halves the error -- gc and 2a*sqrt(gamma) are themselves 2.6 vs 2.6, still cancelling. Not a real fix.

FIX MUST ADDRESS THE NOISE FLOOR. Candidates:
(a) Snap c0 to exactly 0 when |c0| is at or below the rounding noise of the cancelled subtraction, e.g. |c0| <= K * ulp(gc*gc). Directly cancels the FMA artifact and restores CPU/GPU agreement at the source.
(b) Make eps RELATIVE to the conditioning: eps = max(current, K * ulp(max|coeff|)/|c1|), i.e. track the ~1.1e-6 noise floor rather than a fixed 1e-7.
(c) Both. Apply the same change to the Rust f32 mirror so the twin stays a twin.

NOTE this is only partly a fixture artifact. A real transport run has particles sitting on and just off surfaces constantly, so the on-surface case is the norm, not a corner. Also: with coincident:true the eps becomes 1e-5, which WOULD filter 3.12e-7 -- so a caller that correctly flags coincidence escapes the bug.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
FIXED 2026-08-06. Verified on NVIDIA RTX A5000 / NVK GA102 / Vulkan.

TWO CHANGES, applied IDENTICALLY to both sides (shaders/surface_distance.wgsl and the Rust f32 mirror in gpu/surface_distance.rs), because the whole defect was the two drifting apart:

1. SNAP c0 TO ZERO BELOW ITS OWN ROUNDING NOISE.
   c0_raw = gc*gc - 4*a2*gamma
   c0_noise = C0_CANCELLATION_ULPS * F32_EPS * max(|gc*gc|, |4*a2*gamma|)
   c0 = 0 when |c0_raw| <= c0_noise
   Below that threshold the value carries no information -- it is indistinguishable from zero in f32 -- so this removes the FMA-vs-two-rounding divergence at source rather than downstream.

2. MAKE THE ROOT GATE TRACK THE NOISE FLOOR instead of sitting under it.
   eps = max(base_eps, min(c0_noise / |c1|, EPS_CAP))
   A residual perturbation dc0 displaces a simple root near zero by dc0/|c1|. The old fixed 1.0e-7 sat roughly an order of magnitude BELOW the measured f32 noise floor (~1.1e-6) for cm-scale torus geometry, so noise roots always passed. EPS_CAP = 1.0e-3 cm (10 um) stops a near-zero c1 from widening the gate enough to swallow a real crossing.

New shared constants, spelled identically on both sides (WGSL has no f32::EPSILON): F32_EPS = 1.1920929e-7, C0_CANCELLATION_ULPS = 4.0, EPS_CAP = 1.0e-3.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES (all established during investigation, recorded so they are not retried):
- Normalising the quartic: c4 = ga^2 = 1.0 exactly here, it is already monic and all coefficients are O(1). Would change nothing.
- Disabling FMA: naga emits no NoContraction decoration anywhere, so contraction is not controllable from the shader.
- Reformulating c0 as a difference of squares (gc - 2a*sqrt(gamma))(gc + 2a*sqrt(gamma)): gc and 2a*sqrt(gamma) are themselves 2.6 vs 2.6, so it still cancels. Halves the error at best.

RESULT: gpu::surface_distance::tests::gpu_matches_cpu_reference PASSES over all 19440 queries and all 15 surface types. Previously 79 mismatches (XTorus 70, ZTorus 9, YTorus 0, non-torus 0 of 15552). Full crate suite: 197 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored. cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android clean.

NO TOLERANCE WAS LOOSENED -- the test's pass criterion is unchanged at |gpu-cpu| <= 1e-3*(1+|cpu|). The kernel now produces the right answer.

title: GPU torus quartic root-finder disagrees with CPU mirror (spurious near-zero root)

description:
The Wakao correlation was corrected on 2026-08-11 from the transposed `Nu = 2 + 1.1 Re^0.333 Pr^0.6` to the published `Nu = 2 + 1.1 Pr^(1/3) Re^0.6`. The implementing fleet captured AFTER numbers but stopped with the BEFORE baseline outstanding, so the question the whole task existed to answer is still open.

THE QUESTION. Wakao sits on a CALIBRATED CIET path — ciet_heater_v2, the porous-media components, the heater top/bottom heads. The crate CLAUDE.md records that CIET steady-state natural-circulation and isothermal tests agree with published Zweibaum (2015) and Zou et al. (2019) data to within ~6 percent. If a heat-transfer coefficient was calibrated against experiment WHILE the correlation was wrong, the calibration absorbed the error, and correcting the correlation should have moved that agreement.

So: did agreement change? Nobody measured. Three possibilities and they have very different consequences:
1. Agreement unchanged -> the calibrated path was insensitive to Wakao, or the calibration dominates it. Fine, but worth knowing.
2. Agreement degraded -> the calibration WAS masking the error, and re-calibrating against experiment with correct physics is a separate, larger job needing maintainer sign-off. Do NOT re-tune to hide it and do NOT revert the correlation to keep tests green.
3. The tests never exercise Wakao at all -> a coverage finding, and it would explain how a factor-5.84 error at Re = 1000 survived.

HOW TO GET IT. Run the CIET suite on a worktree at the pre-fix commit and compare against the post-fix numbers. Both runs are expensive: the full TUAS lib suite measured 2959.84 s (49 minutes) on this machine, and per CLAUDE.md it must run in PARALLEL, never with --test-threads=1. A killed run is neither a pass nor a fail.

COMPOUNDING FACTOR, see op-lmye: ciet_heater_v2 feeds a HYDRAULIC-diameter Reynolds number to Wakao, which is defined on PARTICLE diameter. So the calibrated path had TWO errors — a transposed correlation and a wrong length scale. Fixing one without the other may move agreement in a confusing direction, and any baseline comparison must say which fixes were in place for each run.

THIS IS A CLASS, NOT AN INCIDENT. The same audit filed op-ctbq (Pr_bulk/Pr_wall swapped in PipeGnielinskiCalibrated - the same transposition class, still latent), op-tidc (Sieder-Tate bounds inverted), op-i7od (LMTD ambient helper sign/panic), and op-a3yi. A correlation module with this many transposition and inversion defects deserves a systematic pass against the published forms, not one fix at a time.
title: TUAS Wakao fix: the BEFORE baseline was never measured, so calibration masking is unresolved

description:
Maintainer report 2026-08-12: htgr_sim_v1 fails too easily because of the steel temperature ceiling in the new nodalised steam generator.

THE LIMIT. TUAS's SolidMaterial::SteelSS304L property tables are tabulated to 1000 K and TUAS PANICS above that rather than returning an error or clamping. The steam generator's tube metal is SteelSS304L, so any transient that drives a metal node past 1000 K kills the physics thread.

MARGIN AT DESIGN: metal sits near 765 K, so about 235 K of headroom. That sounds generous and is not, because the reachable excursions are much larger than 235 K -- a full control-rod withdrawal exposes +16.45 dollars, and with the protection system disarmed (which is currently the DEFAULT, see the RPS toggle) nothing terminates it. The agent that built the exchanger documented this as a known unguarded failure rather than fixing it.

WHY IT FEELS LIKE THE SIMULATOR IS FRAGILE: the failure presents as a hard panic and the restart modal, so an operator exploring a transient gets a dead simulator with no explanation of what they did. That is exactly the class of failure the crash-component reporting and the salt-freeze guard were built to avoid elsewhere -- a recoverable excursion out of the model's valid envelope should PAUSE and explain, not crash.

WHAT A FIX SHOULD LOOK LIKE, in rough order of value:

1. GUARD THE PROPERTY CALL, do not silently clamp. Detect a metal node approaching 1000 K BEFORE calling the property, and park the physics thread with a modal naming the component and the temperature -- the same pattern as salt_freeze_guard in fhr_sim_v2 (detect on the previous step's state, pause, explain, offer recovery). Silently clamping would be worse: it would keep running while the model is outside its data.

2. Consider whether 1000 K is the right ceiling at all. It is a PROPERTY TABLE limit, not a material limit -- 304L stainless does not cease to exist at 727 degC, it just is not tabulated there in TUAS. Extending the table, or using a material whose data covers the range, may be more honest than guarding. Check what TUAS actually carries before assuming.

3. Feed it back into the protection system. A high metal temperature is a legitimate trip signal on a real plant, and the RPS (physics/protection.rs) already has the structure -- it trips on measurable signals with a latching scram. Metal temperature is arguably measurable in a way fuel temperature is not.

NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH THE RPS DEFAULT. The protection system is currently DISARMED by default (maintainer decision, so the steam generator could be studied without a trip cutting transients short). Re-arming it would mask this failure rather than fix it, and the two decisions should be revisited together.

RELATED: the same class of defect was found in the IF97 (p,h) flash, which panics out of Region 5 rather than erroring -- that is what the GUI-timestep bug surfaced. Property libraries in this workspace panic rather than return Result at roughly 40 sites; guarding call sites one at a time is the current approach.
title: SolidColumn steel property tables panic above 1000 K — the SG kills the sim too easily
